title: All Balanced Bracket Strings
statement:
Given n, return every string made of exactly n opening brackets ( and n closing brackets ) that is balanced: read from left to right, the number of ) never exceeds the number of ( seen so far.

Each string must appear once. The strings may be returned in any order.

examples.why: The only way to use one pair.
Five strings. Note "(()())": the pairs are neither all nested nor all side by side.
14 strings. A popular shortcut builds each answer from the n − 1 answers by adding "()" in front, "()" behind, or wrapping in "( )". It works up to n = 3 but never produces "(())(())".

hints: Build the string one character at a time. At any point, which of the two characters are you allowed to add?
You may add ( while you have used fewer than n of them. You may add ) only while it would close something, that is while closes used < opens used.
Backtrack with two counters, opens and closes. When the string reaches length 2n, record it. Those two rules never create a dead end, so every leaf is an answer.

explain.intuition:
Think of the string as a stack you push to and pop from: ( pushes, ) pops. A string is balanced exactly when you never pop an empty stack and the stack is empty at the end. So at each position there are only two questions: can I still push (fewer than n opens used)? Can I pop (something is open)?

Explore both choices recursively. Because a choice is only made when it can still lead to a full answer, the search never wastes time on dead branches: the work is proportional to the output size. The number of answers grows like the Catalan numbers: 1, 2, 5, 14, 42, 132, 429, 1430.
steps: Recurse with the current string, opens used and closes used.
If the length is 2n, record the string and return.
If opens < n, recurse with ( appended and opens + 1.
If closes < opens, recurse with ) appended and closes + 1.
Start from the empty string with both counters at 0.
pitfalls: Allowing ) whenever closes < n. That produces strings like )(, which close before they open.
Building answers from the n − 1 answers by wrapping and concatenating. It misses shapes such as (())(()) and creates duplicates you then have to remove.
Sharing one mutable array for the current string and forgetting to undo the push after each recursive call.

complexity.time: O(4ⁿ / √n), the number of answers times n

solutions.title: Try every string, keep the balanced ones
solutions.idea: There are 2^(2n) strings of length 2n made of ( and ). Check each with a running depth counter.

solutions.title: Backtracking with open and close counts
solutions.idea: Add ( while fewer than n are used; add ) while it closes something. Every complete string is balanced, and every branch reaches one.

solutions.title: Split on the first pair
solutions.idea: Every balanced string is "(" + A + ")" + B, where the first bracket closes after A, and A and B are balanced with i and n − 1 − i pairs. Build answers for every size from the smaller ones.

followups: Return only the count, for n up to 1000 modulo 10⁹ + 7. What recurrence do you use?
Generate the strings in lexicographic order without sorting. Which branch should the recursion try first?
